title: Henderson–Hasselbalch and renal handling of excess HCO₃⁻
guide: pH = pKa + log [HCO₃⁻]/PaCO₂ and [H⁺] = 24 × PaCO₂/HCO₃⁻. A rise in HCO₃⁻ (metabolic alkalosis) leads to a rise in PaCO₂ to keep H⁺ constant. Whether the alkalosis persists depends on the kidney: excess HCO₃⁻ excreted with Cl⁻ conserved means no metabolic alkalosis, whereas failure to excrete it produces metabolic alkalosis.

title: Saline-unresponsive alkalosis: ECF volume expansion and its causes
guide: ECF volume expansion = saline unresponsive metabolic alkalosis with normal urine Cl⁻ (> 40 mEq/L). Major causes by renin–aldosterone pattern: ↓renin/↑aldosterone = primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn's syndrome); ↑renin/↑aldosterone = RAS and renin-secreting tumours; ↓renin/↓aldosterone = Liddle syndrome (gain-of-function ENaC mutation). Other causes: Cushing syndrome (cortisol excess → mineralocorticoid excess), apparent mineralocorticoid excess (blocked cortisol → cortisone step) and glucocorticosteroid remediable aldosteronism (ACTH → aldosterone).

title: The alkalosis triad, urine chloride and the acidosis note
guide: Features triangle: alkalosis with hypokalemia and HTN. ECF volume contraction = secondary hyperreninemic hyperaldosteronism (hypokalemia, alkalosis), ↓GFR (↓urine Cl⁻, ↓urine K⁺) and saline responsive alkalosis, caused by GI (vomiting, NG aspiration) or renal factors (diuretics, post hypercapnia, cystic fibrosis, Mg²⁺/K⁺ depletion, Bartter, Gitelman). The urine chloride ladder reads low (< 25 mEq/L: GI loss, post hypercapnia, cystic fibrosis, late-phase diuretics), normal (> 40 mEq/L: ECF volume expansion) and high (renal loss: early-phase diuretics, Bartter, Gitelman). The closing note splits metabolic acidosis into acid generation (high anion gap) and alkali loss — GI causes NAGMA with a negative UAG (VIPoma) versus renal causes NAGMA with a positive UAG (RTA).
